title: Experimental remediation scheduler with safety gates and playback harness
author: Marisol Rivera
description:
Motivation: on-call engineers still spend manual cycles validating remediation steps against live or semi-live traffic. This PR introduces an experimental remediation scheduler that can 'play back' a recorded incident trace into an isolated sandbox, run candidate remediation sequences, and surface safety metrics (blast radius estimate, confidence, latency impact) before any live rollout. The goal is to reduce human toil and shorten mean-time-to-safe-repair while keeping automatic actions gated behind clear safety checks.

What this change does:
 - Adds a playback sandbox (pkg/playback) that replays core signals (alert timeline, representative queries) against a local, instrumented environment. Replays are deterministic and time-accelerated.
 - Introduces a remediation scheduler (cmd/incident-bot/scheduler.go) that can: 1) schedule dry-run playbacks, 2) score remediation sequences with a safety policy, 3) enqueue safe canary rollouts.
 - Implements safety gates (configurable policies) that require: blast radius <= threshold, rollback path verified, and a successful smoke-check within the sandbox.
 - Adds a simple UI card + endpoint to trigger/inspect a playback run (webapp/...).
 - Adds telemetry and structured evaluation output to Redwood's observability (events: playback.started, playback.result, remediation.score).

Checklist:
 - [x] Playback harness core (deterministic replayer and mock adapters)
 - [x] Scheduler integration and queueing
 - [x] Safety gate evaluator with policy templates
 - [x] UI endpoint and minimal card for on-call workflows
 - [x] Unit tests for policy checks and scheduler state machine
 - [x] Integration test harness (runs in CI with mocked external services)

Backward compatibility & safety: This feature is behind a feature flag (FEATURE_PLAYBACK_SCHEDULER) and defaults to off. No live automated remediations are enabled by default; the scheduler only enqueues canary rollouts to a dry-run namespace unless a user explicitly promotes a remediation after review.

Example usage (description-only): run a recorded trace and evaluate a remediation sequence:
  $ rbcli incidents playback --trace trace-2025-08-24 --remediation fix-high-cpu.yaml --simulate

High-level commits:
 - Add playback engine and deterministic clock
 - Implement remediation scheduler and queue worker
 - Safety policy evaluator + policy templates
 - Add UI endpoint and lightweight card
 - Tests + CI integration tweaks

Files changed (high-level):
 - cmd/incident-bot/scheduler.go
 - pkg/playback/replayer.go
 - pkg/playback/sandbox_adapter.go
 - pkg/remediation/policy_evaluator.go
 - webapp/src/cards/playback-card.tsx
 - deploy/k8s/playback-crd.yaml
 - test/integration/playback_e2e_test.go

Small illustrative snippet (sandbox adapter contract):
  // sandbox_adapter.go: Replay interface
  type SandboxAdapter interface {
    StartSandbox(ctx) error
    ReplayEvent(ctx, ev) error
    SmokeCheck(ctx) (SmokeResult, error)
    TearDown(ctx) error
  }

Why this is different: existing auto-remediation flows at Redwood are conservative but rely on live trial-and-error. This introduces a reproducible, auditable runway for validating remediations and recording safety metrics before any live impact.

Notes on scope: this is explicitly labeled experimental; follow-up work will add richer trace sampling, automatic rollback verification, and integration with on-call approval flows.
commits: 3 commits: add playback engine; add scheduler + worker; wire policy evaluator and UI endpoint
ci_checks: integration: fail (flaky e2e on first run) -> rerun -> pass
review_conversation: Ethan Rosen (reviewer): Nice work on the deterministic replayer. A couple of things: (1) can we make the default time-acceleration configurable per-playback? (2) the sandbox adapter needs stronger resource isolation (cpu/memory limits) to avoid noisy neighbor effects on shared CI runners.

Marisol Rivera (author): Added timeAcceleration in the playback config and documented it. For CI we added a lightweight cgroup wrapper for the sandbox and additional env flags so runs in shared CI enforce caps. See pkg/playback/sandbox_adapter.go changes.

Priya Kumar (reviewer): We should ensure the policy templates are reviewable by SRE/CS teams; recommend adding a curated set and a validation CLI. Also flagging that telemetry payloads must not include PII — verify scrubbers run in the replayer path.

Marisol Rivera (author): Policy templates added under deploy/playback/policies; added a validation step in test/integration and a scrubber pass that runs during replay. Updated docs with non-inclusive data policy and examples.

Liam O'Connor (approver): Integration tests are flakey-less on reruns; reviewed policy evaluator and sandbox contract. Approving pending a small follow-up to annotate telemetry samples with a "playback_id" for easier correlation.
release_notes: Experimental: add playback scheduler and safety-gated remediation dry-run capability (feature-flagged). Intended for early SRE experimentation; not enabled by default.
